messages.subject: Changing format of numbers in legend in rworldmap
messages.subject_clean: Changing format of numbers in legend in rworldmap
messages.body_plain:
Hello, I was wondering how to change the numbers in a legend so that they are either percents or not in scientific expression.  Also is it possible to override the range?  For example, the legends defaults to the lowest and highest values, anyway to override this so it is more "clean"?
Thank you,
Matt

messages.subject: Kaliningrad, European Turkey missing
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to use ggplot2 to make nicer rworldmap plots, based on the code I found here: http://editerna.free.fr/wp/?p=130

The plot generated by the code below shows that Kaliningrad (Russian part in Europe) and Thrace (European Turkey) are missing. Perhaps because of the discontinuity with the main polygon? Is there any way to make these parts reappear?

On a related note, I noticed that worldMap$NAME[207] is NA.

## load packages
library(ggplot2)
library(rworldmap)

## identify countries
worldMap <- getMap()
show <- which(worldMap$NAME %in% c("Russia", "Turkey", "Greece"))

## convert to data.frame
showCoords <-
  lapply(show,
         function(x) {
           df <- data.frame(worldMap@polygons[[x]]@Polygons[[1]]@coords)
           df$region <- as.character(worldMap$NAME[x])
           colnames(df) <- list("long", "lat", "region")
           return(df)
         })
showCoords <- do.call("rbind", showCoords)

## gplot
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data = showCoords,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = region))

messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] Kaliningrad, European Turkey missing
messages.body_plain:
It's probably an issue with the underlying map imported from Natural
Earth (http://www.naturalearthdata.com/downloads/10m-cultural-vectors/10m-admin-0-countries/).
The borders are not compliant with the views of the UN General
Assembly, I already mentioned this to Andy in the past. See th
disclaimer by the people who compile Natural Earth: "Natural Earth
Vector draws boundaries of countries according to defacto status. We
show who actually controls the situation on the ground. Please feel
free to mashup our disputed area themes to match your particular
political outlook."

Natural Earth is "supported by NACIS (North American Cartographic
Information Society)". Personally I suspect that their maps often
reflect the viewpoint of (some people in) the United States :-( Hence
the fact they "forgot" Kaliningrad...

Regards,
   JB

messages.subject_clean: [rworldmap group] Changing format of numbers in legend in rworldmap
messages.body_plain:
Hi Matt,

Please have a look at the rworldmap vignette and also at the manpages:
you should find your way drawing first a map without a lengend
(addLegend = F), and then use the object created by the call to the
mapping function in order to get the proper parameters for the
function addMapLegend, and specify additional parameters to tweak your
legend, for example the options sigFigs and digits. See the help on
addMapLegend.

Example from the vignette:

mapParams <- mapCountryData( sPDF, nameColumnToPlot="BIODIVERSITY",
addLegend=FALSE )
do.call( addMapLegend, c(mapParams, legendWidth=0.5, legendMar = 2))

It will maybe not aoutomatically give you what you want, but maybe you
can also process the data upstream, for instance if you want
percentages you should multiply the data (ratio) by 100 before
proceeding with the map...

Regards,
   JB
